stock: 205/75R15, 215/75R15 or 225/75R15 (SE, X, Sport, depending on year)

max_tire.note: Jeep put 31-inch LT245/75R16s on the Rubicon from the factory, and Four Wheel Trends puts the stock-suspension limit at 31x10.50-15 (may rub at full flex). Check wheel backspacing so the tires stay inside the flares.
Quadratec's buyer's guide: a 2 in spacer lift typically accommodates up to 31 in tires.
Quadratec's buyer's guide: up to 33 in on its stage-2 suspension lift, 35 in on a long-arm setup. Plan a regear from the stock ratio (3.07 on many 4.0 manuals, per Jeep's 2005–06 specs).

items.title: Airbag control module software
items.summary: A software error could delay airbag deployment in some crashes.

items.title: Inadvertent airbag deployment at shut-off
items.summary: The circuit design could fire the airbag when the ignition is switched off.

items.title: Driver airbag clockspring
items.summary: The clockspring harness can break when the wheel is turned to full lock.

items.title: Front seat-belt turning loops
items.summary: Shoulder-belt turning-loop anchors were not properly heat-treated.

items.title: Brake booster vacuum diaphragm
items.summary: The power brake booster vacuum reservoir diaphragm can split or tear; dealers checked the booster date code and replaced suspect units.

items.title: Instrument-panel ground screws
items.summary: The instrument-panel wiring ground screws can loosen; dealers re-drilled and reinstalled them.

items.title: Ignition switch water intrusion
items.summary: Water can get into the ignition switch and short it; dealers fitted a redesigned switch.

items.title: 4.0 L manifold debris at cylinder 3
items.summary: Debris could collect between the manifolds at cylinder 3; dealers fitted a manifold shield.

items.title: 42RLE park pawl anchor shaft
items.summary: An improperly installed cup plug can let the shaft move so the transmission won't go into Park; dealers added a retaining bracket.

items.title: Six-speed clutch master cylinder rod
items.summary: The linkage rod can break so the clutch won't disengage; replaced free.

items.title: Clutch pedal interlock switch
items.summary: Switch springs can break, letting the engine start in gear without the clutch pressed; switch replaced free.

timeline.change: TJ launches (shown January 1996, in showrooms April 1996) with coil springs at all four corners and round headlights; 2.5 L four or 4.0 L six with the AX-5/AX-15 manuals or 3-speed automatics

Early-TJ teething: SlashGear notes seven recalls for 1997 and early engine-computer, fuel-system and brake bugs; Driving Line says cracked 4.0 exhaust manifolds are most common on 1997–2000 trucks; Off Road Xtreme says the early cowl vent leaks water onto the floors, a design Jeep revised on later TJs
NV3550 five-speed replaces the AX-15 behind the 4.0
Thicker, more durable factory soft-top fabric; 60th Anniversary Edition
Mid-cycle update: 42RLE four-speed automatic replaces the 3-speed, 2.4 L replaces the 2.5 L four, revised interior. Rubicon arrives with Dana 44s front and rear, air lockers and the 4:1 NV241OR
Long-wheelbase Wrangler Unlimited (LJ) joins the range
NSG370 six-speed manual replaces the five-speeds
Final year: 65th Anniversary and Golden Eagle editions; production ends July 2006

identify.intro: Rubicon badges, decals and axles are easy to bolt onto a Sport, so check the VIN and the hardware before paying a Rubicon price.

items.head: VIN trim code
items.body: All TJ VINs start 1J4FA. The 6th character marks the trim: 2 SE, 3 X, 4 Sport, 5 Sahara, 6 Rubicon. In BaT-listed VINs we checked, the 7th was 9 on short-wheelbase trucks and 4 on the Unlimited (a Rubicon reads 1J4FA69…, an Unlimited Rubicon 1J4FA64…), but NHTSA's decoder doesn't separate the two, so confirm by wheelbase.

items.head: VIN engine code
items.body: The 8th character is the engine: S is the 4.0 L six, P the 2.5 L four and 1 the 2.4 L four (NHTSA decoder: 1J4FA29P… is a 2.5 L SE, 1J4FA291… a 2.4 L SE).

items.head: Real Rubicon hardware
items.body: Front and rear Dana 44s with air-actuated lockers and dash switches, the Rock-Trac NV241OR transfer case with a 4:1 low range, diamond-plate rocker guards and 16-inch alloys on LT245/75R16 tires.

items.head: Rear axle
items.body: Sport, SE and X trucks normally have the weaker Dana 35. A Dana 44 rear was optional on Sport and Sahara, sometimes with a Trac-Lok limited slip. The axle tag and cover shape tell you which one you have.

items.head: Transmission by year
items.body: Manual 4.0 trucks used the AX-15 (1997–99), the NV3550 (2000–04) and the NSG370 six-speed (2005–06). Automatics are the 32RH 3-speed (1997–2002) and the 42RLE 4-speed (2003–06).

items.head: Special editions
items.body: The 2003 Tomb Raider Rubicon has a serial-numbered badge, red seat belts and Bright Silver paint. The 2001 60th Anniversary came only in black or Silverstone.

capability.v: 2,000 lb (907 kg) 4.0 L · 1,000 lb (454 kg) 2.4 L and 4.0 automatic with base 3.73 axle
8.6–9.1 in (218–231 mm) at the rear axle

values.intro: Tidy TJs are now firmly collectible. Rubicons, low-mile originals and 2005–06 six-speed trucks bring the strongest money, and heavily modified ones vary wildly.
values.note: Based on 256 short-wheelbase TJ sales on Bring a Trailer from April 2025 to October 2026: median ≈$15,500, middle half ≈$11,000–20,500. Rubicons had a median of ≈$20,000. The best stock result was a 21k-mile 2006 Rubicon six-speed at $39,000; engine-swapped builds sold for up to $57,000.
